issues.sourceClaim: The slide says parallel motion ensures uniform gripping force without specifying contact, pressure or mechanical symmetry conditions.
issues.qualification: Motion symmetry is not by itself a force-balance measurement.

issues.sourceClaim: The printed purple and magenta hue intervals share 155 if both boundaries are inclusive; no tie-breaking rule is supplied.
issues.qualification: Hue 155 is included in both printed purple and magenta ranges, and S,V pass.

issues.sourceClaim: The slide prints hue upper bound 180 without distinguishing a threshold bound from the 0–179 ordinary 8-bit OpenCV hue encoding.
issues.qualification: A threshold bound can lie just outside the encoded hue domain without requiring a pixel with hue 180.

issues.sourceClaim: The component slide loosely calls OpenShowVar a Python library while the bibliography separately names the original client and py_openshowvar port.
issues.qualification: The references distinguish the original client project and a separately named Python port.

issues.sourceClaim: The source calls the communication arrangement real-time without supplying deadlines, worst-case jitter or a demonstrated timing guarantee.
issues.qualification: Continuous polling/exchange is not a demonstrated hard-real-time timing guarantee.

Four-point TCP calculation estimates a point and requires sufficient orientation diversity; exact/noiseless accuracy is not assumed.
No original executable Python or KRL listing is provided in this lecture. robosync.src is a described component, not retrieved or executed code.
No external controller connection, hardware operation, original video execution or runtime success rate is claimed.
OpenCV is absent in the permitted default environment. No install or restricted environment is used; numerical models and independent simple algorithms are explicitly added.
Colour/depth registration, distortion correction, units, physical marker geometry and tool/grasp pose are necessary explicit premises.
Named safe heights and the conceptual sequence are not complete hardware safety or collision certification.
